Chapter 9: Giving Back and Redefining Success
When you reach a certain level of success, a whole new set of questions comes up. What does it really mean to "make it"? Is it just about the money in your account, the size of your team, or seeing your name in the headlines? Or is there something deeper—something about meaning, about legacy, about giving back to others?
As the company started to grow, so did the feeling of responsibility. The team began to look past the app, past the business, and out into the world around them. There were causes that truly mattered—like education, access to technology, and opening doors for young people. The big question quickly became: How can we use what we’ve built to actually make a difference?
At first, it was simple. Donating old devices to local schools. Mentoring kids who were curious about technology. Sponsoring small community events. But as the company’s reach expanded, so did its ability to create real change. Suddenly, there were partnerships with nonprofits, scholarships for up-and-coming entrepreneurs, and programs teaching coding in communities that had never had those opportunities before. Each new initiative was a chance to give back—a way to pay forward the help and encouragement that had made their own journey possible.
Of course, it wasn’t always smooth sailing. Not every project worked out. Some ideas fizzled, some efforts hit resistance. But the lessons they'd learned in those tough early days—things like resilience, curiosity, and the courage to just try—turned out to be just as valuable in giving as they were in building.
Redefining success meant looking beyond just the numbers. It meant asking tough questions about impact, about values, about what kind of company—and honestly, what kind of people—they wanted to become. There were debates, disagreements, even a few moments of real uncertainty. But alongside all of that, there was a growing sense of purpose. A belief that business could actually be a force for good.
The journey wasn’t just about becoming the youngest billionaire in the room. It was about using that platform to open doors for others, to create opportunities, and to leave the world just a little bit better than it was before.
The iPhone, which once stood for personal ambition, became a tool for collective impact. The story wasn’t just about one person’s dream anymore. It was about what happens when you share that dream, expand it, and use it to lift others up.
